landmarks.text: A city of grey towers, palaces and spies on a terrace above the river.

landmarks.name: The Frontier Forts
landmarks.text: Forts in the northern passes, facing the demon lands.

landmarks.name: The Barracks Pledge
landmarks.text: The founders' oath carved under the capital's barracks.

hooks: An imperial spy wants an outsider to carry a message through the frontier, one that cannot be trusted to a legion courier.
A fallen fort's survivors are hiding in the mountains, and the legion has written them off.
The guild's receptionist from Brindlewick has been seen in the capital, and someone wants to know why.
reg_vharlen.senses: Polished steel and horse sweat; marching drums; ink and wax in the ministries; the alarm horn's long note.

reg_gearholm.name: Gearholm
reg_gearholm.summary: A clockwork city stacked on a mountain, and an Undercity where the steam and the poor collect. Cogmaw the Gremlin Engine King is taking it apart from the bottom up.
reg_gearholm.echo: Gearholm's founders built the city's engines and lost the instructions within a generation.
reg_gearholm.overview: Gearholm is a city of clockwork and steam that climbs the side of a mountain in tiers, where gnome and human inventors have built machines for everything: lifts, rail-carts, looms, pumps, automaton porters and a clock that tells the time in seven cities at once. The upper city is bright, clean and proud of itself. The Undercity, where the steam, the smoke and the poor collect, is dark, loud and forgotten. Something down there has started eating the city from the bottom up.
reg_gearholm.geography: Gearholm is built on the southern face of a mountain, its tiers linked by lifts, funicular railways and spiral stairs. The upper tiers are terraces of workshops, academies and mansions with gardens and glass roofs. The middle tiers are factories and markets. The lower tiers vanish into permanent steam, and below them the Undercity runs deep into the mountain: a maze of tunnels, pipes, boilers and slums built around the Great Engines that power the whole city. No one living has seen all of them.
reg_gearholm.ecology: Pigeons, rats and steam-moths are the city's wildlife, along with the clockwork birds that inventors release for fun and never recover. Gremlins, little mechanical vermin that eat metal and breed inside machines, have always infested the Undercity, and the city has always employed gremlin-catchers to keep them down. Lately the gremlins have stopped behaving like vermin. They are organised, and they are building.
reg_gearholm.peoples: The people of Gearholm are gnomes and humans, with a scattering of dwarves who came for the work and stayed for the arguments. Upper-city folk are inventors, engineers, academics and merchants, brilliant, competitive and a little arrogant. Undercity folk are labourers, boiler-tenders, scavengers and gremlin-catchers, tough, resourceful and bitterly aware of who keeps the city running. Ideas move up the mountain; credit rarely moves down it.
reg_gearholm.powerAndTrade: Gearholm is ruled by a council of guild-masters, one for each great industry, elected by their guilds. The council meets in the Clock Tower and votes by pulling levers. The Undercity has no seat on it. The economy rests on machines, clocks, engines, tools and patents, and Gearholm's patents are worth more than many kingdoms' treasuries.
reg_gearholm.faithAndCustoms: The people honour the day-gods, especially Kael, whom inventors claim as their patron. Undercity folk keep a quieter faith in the Great Engines themselves: they leave oil and bolts at the engine shrines and speak to the machines as if they could hear. A machine is never broken up without a word of thanks.

history.now: Cogmaw's gremlins have taken the lowest levels of the Undercity and are moving upward, stripping pipes, rails and lifts as they go. The council wants the Undercity sealed off, with its people inside.
history.parents: Within living memory a Great Engine exploded and killed hundreds in the Undercity. The council blamed the boiler-tenders, and the boiler-tenders have never forgiven it.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the founders' instructions for the Great Engines were lost in a fire, and the city has been maintaining machines it does not fully understand ever since.
history.ancient: Gearholm's founders built the city's engines and lost the instructions within a generation.

reg_gearholm.tyrant: Cogmaw, the Gremlin Engine King, began as an ordinary gremlin that crawled inside one of the Great Engines and never came out. It ate, grew and merged with the engine until it became a single thing: a vast, living machine that thinks. It commands the gremlins as its body commands its gears, and it wants the whole mountain as its body. It is very clever and very hungry, and it has found the founders' lost instructions inside its own engine.

settlements.name: Gearholm Undercity
settlements.text: The tunnels, boilers and slums beneath the mountain, home of the city's labourers and of the Great Engines.

landmarks.name: The Great Engines
landmarks.text: The enormous machines at the mountain's heart that power the whole city.

landmarks.name: The Clock Tower
landmarks.text: A tower whose clock tells the time in seven cities, where the council meets.

landmarks.name: The Long Funicular
landmarks.text: A railway that climbs from the lowest tier to the highest, and is the only safe way between them.

hooks: An upper-city inventor needs a part that exists only in the gremlin-held Undercity, and she will pay a fortune not to go herself.
A boiler-tender's union wants proof that the council knew about Cogmaw and did nothing.
A child in the Undercity has befriended a gremlin that says it does not want to be part of the king.
reg_gearholm.senses: Steam, coal and machine oil; the clank and whir of a thousand gears; whistles and bells on every hour; something small and metal scurrying in the dark.

reg_cinderhole.name: Cinderhole
reg_cinderhole.summary: A city in a smoking crater, built inside caves that are never dark and never clean. Cinderlord Vasque rules the smoke and everything sold through it.
reg_cinderhole.echo: Cinderhole was a mine until it caught fire. It never stopped burning, so people moved in.
reg_cinderhole.overview: Cinderhole is a city built inside a smoking crater, in caves that are never dark and never clean. It was a mine until the coal seams caught fire and never stopped burning, and the people who stayed learned to live in the heat, the smoke and the endless glow. It is a city of smugglers, alchemists, refugees and fortune-seekers, where anything can be bought and everyone is hiding something. Cinderlord Vasque rules the smoke, and everything sold through it.
reg_cinderhole.geography: The crater is a vast pit in a range of barren hills, wreathed in smoke that rises day and night. Fires burn in the coal seams beneath it, and vents in the rock leak heat and fumes. The city is built into the crater's walls and the caves behind them, terraces and tunnels lit by the glow of the fires. Great chimneys carved into the rock carry the worst of the smoke away.
reg_cinderhole.ecology: Little lives in the crater except fire beetles, ash moths, smoke bats and the people. Fire elementals and smoke spirits drift up from the burning seams. Food, water and nearly everything else must be brought in by caravan.
reg_cinderhole.peoples: The people of Cinderhole are miners, alchemists, smugglers, mercenaries and refugees from every land who have nowhere else to go. They are tough, wary and fiercely independent. Smoke-masks are worn by everyone, and a person's mask says more about them than their face.
reg_cinderhole.powerAndTrade: Cinderhole is ruled by the Cinderlord, who controls the smoke vents and the chimneys and therefore who can breathe. Under him, gangs and guilds compete for territory. The economy rests on coal, alchemy, smuggling and the black market, and Cinderhole is the place to buy anything that cannot be bought elsewhere.
reg_cinderhole.faithAndCustoms: The people honour the day-gods quietly and the fire openly. They believe the burning seams are a punishment for the old miners' greed, and that the fire will go out only when the debt is paid.

history.now: Vasque has begun closing chimneys to punish districts that resist him, and people are choking in their homes.
history.parents: Within living memory a great fire-storm swept the crater and killed thousands, and Vasque rose to power promising it would never happen again.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time Cinderhole was a mine, and the miners dug too deep.
history.ancient: Cinderhole was a mine until it caught fire. It never stopped burning, so people moved in.

reg_cinderhole.tyrant: Cinderlord Vasque, the Smoke Mage, is a human mage who has mastered the smoke and fire of the crater. He controls the vents and the chimneys with his magic, and he can choke a district or burn it at will. He sees himself as a ruler who keeps order in a city that would otherwise tear itself apart. He is not wrong about the city, and he is utterly wrong about himself.

settlements.name: Cinderhole
settlements.text: The city in the smoking crater, built into its walls and the caves behind them.

landmarks.name: The Great Chimneys
landmarks.text: Chimneys carved into the crater wall to carry the smoke away.

landmarks.name: The Burning Seams
landmarks.text: The coal seams that have burned for generations.

landmarks.name: The Mask Market
landmarks.text: A market where smoke-masks are sold, traded and stolen.

hooks: A district's chimney has been closed, and its people need someone to open it.
An alchemist claims to have a way to put out the burning seams, and every gang in the city wants her dead.
A refugee family wants to get out of the crater, and Vasque has forbidden it.
reg_cinderhole.senses: Smoke that stings the eyes; the roar of the fires below; sweat and ash; the hiss of breath through a mask.

reg_bastion.name: Bastion
reg_bastion.summary: Ring upon ring of walls on an open steppe, the last stop before the horde lands. Thrakka, Sabretooth Khan rides against the outer ring.
reg_bastion.echo: Bastion builds a new ring every time the horde breaks the outermost one. There are many rings.
reg_bastion.overview: Bastion is a city of walls on an open steppe, built in rings, one inside the other, each one raised after the horde broke the last. It is the last stop before the horde lands and the shield of everything behind it. Its people are soldiers, builders and farmers who till the fields between the rings. Thrakka, Sabretooth Khan of the Steppe Horde, rides against the outer ring.
reg_bastion.geography: The steppe around Bastion is flat, open and windswept, with nothing to stop a cavalry charge. The city sits on a low rise, its rings of walls spreading outward like ripples in a pond. Fields, pastures and villages fill the spaces between the rings, and the oldest, innermost ring encloses the citadel. Beyond the outermost ring, the steppe stretches north to the horde lands.
reg_bastion.ecology: The steppe supports grass, wildflowers, horses, antelope and wolves, and sabretooth cats, the horde's mounts, hunt there. Within the rings the land is farmed intensively, and every scrap of food is precious during a siege.
reg_bastion.peoples: The people of Bastion are soldiers, masons, farmers and smiths. They are stoic, practical and fiercely loyal to the city. Every child learns to lay stone and to hold a spear. Their humour is dark, and their songs are about walls.
reg_bastion.powerAndTrade: Bastion is ruled by a Warden chosen by the captains of the rings. Each ring has its own captain, and the outermost ring's captain is the most honoured and the most likely to die. The city trades grain, horses and stone with the south and depends on it for iron and supplies.
reg_bastion.faithAndCustoms: The people honour the day-gods and the walls, which they believe hold the spirits of the builders. A stone from the last broken ring is built into each new one.

history.now: Thrakka's horde is besieging the outermost ring, and the masons are already laying the foundations of the next.
history.parents: Within living memory the horde broke two rings in a single summer, and the city nearly fell.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time Bastion had half as many rings, and the city was a fort.
history.ancient: Bastion builds a new ring every time the horde breaks the outermost one. There are many rings.

reg_bastion.tyrant: Thrakka, Sabretooth Khan of the Steppe Horde, is a beastkin warlord who rides a giant sabretooth cat at the head of a horde of riders and beasts. He believes the steppe belongs to the horde and that Bastion is a wound in it. He has sworn to break every ring.

settlements.name: Bastion outer ring
settlements.text: The outermost ring of walls, its villages and fields, the front line of the siege.

landmarks.name: The Citadel
landmarks.text: The innermost ring, the oldest part of the city.

landmarks.name: The Broken Rings
landmarks.text: The ruins of rings the horde has broken, now the foundations of new walls.

landmarks.name: The Stone of Founding
landmarks.text: A stone from the first wall, built into every new ring.

hooks: The outermost ring's captain needs scouts to find out how the horde breaks the walls so quickly.
A mason has found a flaw in the new ring's foundations, and someone put it there.
A horde rider has deserted and wants to tell the Warden something.
reg_bastion.senses: Stone dust and woodsmoke; the ring of masons' hammers; war drums on the steppe; the low growl of great cats.

reg_everdusk.name: Everdusk
reg_everdusk.summary: An endless twilight forest where fey courts hold revels in the glades. The Briar King of the Winter Court wants the Summer Court's last glade.
reg_everdusk.echo: The courts made the dusk to settle an argument about whether it was day or night. They are still arguing.
reg_everdusk.overview: Everdusk is a forest of endless twilight, where the sun never fully rises or sets and the fey courts hold revels in the glades. Politeness is law here, thanks are debts and every bargain binds. The Summer Court and the Winter Court have argued for as long as the forest has existed. The Briar King of the Winter Court wants the Summer Court's last glade.
reg_everdusk.geography: The forest is a vast, ancient woodland of oak, ash and thorn, lit by a perpetual dusk. Glades open among the trees, each one the seat of a fey lord. Rivers run silver, and paths change depending on who walks them. The Summer Court's glades are warm and golden; the Winter Court's are cold and blue.
reg_everdusk.ecology: Deer, foxes, owls and nightingales live in the forest, along with pixies, sprites, dryads and fey beasts of every kind. Plants grow strangely, flowering and fruiting at once. Time flows differently in the glades.
reg_everdusk.peoples: The fey of Everdusk are beautiful, capricious and bound by rules no mortal fully understands. Mortals who live in or near the forest are woodcutters, hunters and changelings, and they know to be very careful with their words.
reg_everdusk.powerAndTrade: The forest is divided between the Summer and Winter Courts, each ruled by a monarch. The courts are bound by ancient agreements and constantly test them. Mortal trade with the fey is dangerous but lucrative: fey goods, enchantments and secrets for mortal names, memories and years.
reg_everdusk.faithAndCustoms: Mortals honour the day-gods and leave offerings for the fey at the forest's edge. Never say thank you to a fey, and never give your name.

history.now: The Briar King's thorns are swallowing the Summer Court's glades, and only one remains. The Summer Court has begun to beg mortals for help, which is unprecedented.
history.parents: Within living memory a mortal child was stolen from the forest's edge and returned as an adult, with no memory of where she had been.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the courts held a great treaty that divided the forest in two.
history.ancient: The courts made the dusk to settle an argument about whether it was day or night. They are still arguing.

reg_everdusk.tyrant: The Briar King, Lord of the Winter Court, is a fey lord of thorns, ice and cold beauty. He believes the Summer Court is weak and the forest should be his. His thorns grow wherever he walks, and his bargains are cruel.

settlements.name: Summer Court glades
settlements.text: The last glades of the Summer Court, warm and golden, home of the Hour That Isn't.

landmarks.name: The Last Glade
landmarks.text: The Summer Court's final glade, ringed by encroaching thorns.

landmarks.name: The Thorn Throne
landmarks.text: The Briar King's seat.

landmarks.name: The Edge Stones
landmarks.text: Stones at the forest's edge where offerings are left.

hooks: The Summer Court wants a mortal champion, and its terms are generous, perhaps too generous.
A woodcutter's daughter has been invited to a fey revel, and her father wants her back before dawn.
A mortal who made a bargain with the Briar King wants to break it.
reg_everdusk.senses: Honey and frost; music that never stops; the rustle of thorns; light that is always just about to change.

reg_apu_highlands.name: Apu Highlands
reg_apu_highlands.summary: Terrace cities climb mountains that were carved by hand, though no one knows whose. Ukhu-Tal, the first stone giant ever made, has woken to see what was done with them.
reg_apu_highlands.echo: Highland families keep knotted cords recording every terrace. The oldest cords record a giant's name.
reg_apu_highlands.overview: The Apu Highlands are a range of high green mountains carved by hand, from valley floor to cloud line, into tens of thousands of terraces. Their people farm those terraces, herd llamas along stone roads and keep their history on knotted cords that only a few can still read. Nobody knows who carved the mountains; the highlanders say the mountains carved themselves for their children. The oldest cords record a giant's name, and the giant has woken up.
reg_apu_highlands.geography: The highlands are steep and immense, their slopes cut into stepped terraces held up by walls of fitted stone so precise that a knife blade cannot slip between the blocks. Rivers fall through deep gorges, crossed by rope bridges that are rewoven every year. Stone roads with thousands of steps link the terrace cities, and relay huts stand along them a day's run apart. Above the terraces rise bare grey peaks capped with snow, and on the tallest stands the Giant's Bed, a flat summit shaped like a sleeping body.
reg_apu_highlands.ecology: Llamas and alpacas graze the upper terraces and carry loads along the roads, condors ride the thermals, pumas hunt vicuña in the high grass and hummingbirds feed on the terrace flowers. Each terrace makes its own little climate, and the highlanders grow hundreds of kinds of potato, maize, quinoa and beans at different heights. Stone giants sleep in the mountains, and the earth tremors that the highlanders call the mountains turning in their sleep are, the cord-keepers say, exactly that.
reg_apu_highlands.peoples: The highlanders are farmers, herders, masons, weavers, runners and cord-keepers. They are communal, hard-working and quietly proud, and they measure a person's worth by the walls they have helped mend. Every family owes a share of labour to the community, and work days are feasts. The cord-keepers are a respected, dwindling order, and young highlanders who leave for the coast rarely come back to learn the knots.
reg_apu_highlands.powerAndTrade: The terrace cities are ruled by a lord in the highest city, advised by the heads of the great families. Labour, not coin, is the main tax, and the roads, bridges and walls are maintained by everyone in turn. Wool, potatoes, dried meat, medicines and fine stonework are traded down the mountains for salt, fish, cotton and metal. The relay runners carry messages across the highlands in a few days.
reg_apu_highlands.faithAndCustoms: The highlanders honour the day-gods and the mountains themselves, which they call the apus, the lords. Every peak has a shrine where offerings of coca leaf, maize beer and woven cloth are left. A wall that falls is mourned like a person, and rebuilt by the whole community.

history.now: Ukhu-Tal has woken on the Giant's Bed and walks the terraces, and the walls break where he steps. He has not yet harmed anyone on purpose, but the terraces are falling, and the harvest with them.
history.parents: Within living memory a great earthquake shook the highlands for three days, and the terraces held; the lowland cities fell.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the cord-keepers could still read every cord in the Cord House, including the oldest ones.
history.ancient: Highland families keep knotted cords recording every terrace. The oldest cords record a giant's name.

reg_apu_highlands.tyrant: Ukhu-Tal, Stone Giant of the First Making, is the first stone giant ever made and the mason of the highlands. He carved the first terraces, taught their making to the first people and lay down on the summit to rest when the work was done. He has woken to find the terraces covered in people, his work patched with other stones and his name forgotten. He walks the terraces looking for the walls he made, and he breaks the ones he did not. He does not know whether he is angry or proud, and someone who can read the oldest cords might be able to tell him.

settlements.name: Terrace cities
settlements.text: Cities of fitted stone built on the terraces, linked by stone roads and relay huts.

landmarks.name: The Great Terraces
landmarks.text: Tens of thousands of stepped fields climbing from the valley floor to the clouds.

landmarks.name: The Cord House
landmarks.text: The hall where the oldest knotted records are kept, many of them unread for generations.

landmarks.name: The Giant's Bed
landmarks.text: The flat summit where Ukhu-Tal slept, still bearing the shape of his body.

hooks: The last cord-keeper who might read the oldest cord is dying in a lowland city, and someone has to bring her home.
Ukhu-Tal has spoken to a child herding llamas, and she is the only person he will talk to.
A terrace wall has collapsed onto a village, and a family is trapped under the stones.
reg_apu_highlands.senses: Thin cold air and woodsmoke; llama bells on the stone roads; maize beer and roasted potatoes; the deep grinding of stone on stone.

reg_lustrine_shores.name: Lustrine Shores
reg_lustrine_shores.summary: Beaches of moon-glass where the tide leaves light behind it. Ilyanthe the Moon Harvester gathers that light for the red moon.
reg_lustrine_shores.echo: The glass began washing in after the red moon rose. The fishers' songs changed key that same year.
reg_lustrine_shores.overview: The Lustrine Shores are beaches of glittering moon-glass, where every tide leaves light behind it. Their people are glass-gatherers, lamp-makers and fishers, and their villages glow at night like scattered stars. The glass began washing in after the red moon rose, and nobody knows where it comes from. Ilyanthe, the Moon Harvester, gathers that light for the red moon.
reg_lustrine_shores.geography: The shores are long beaches of fine sand mixed with fragments of glowing glass, backed by dunes, salt marshes and pine woods. The tides here are higher than anywhere else, pulled by both moons. At low tide, great flats of glass shine for miles. The villages stand on the dunes above the tideline.
reg_lustrine_shores.ecology: Crabs, shorebirds, seals and fish live along the shores, and many of them have begun to glow. Glass-shrimp feed on the light in the moon-glass, and glass-gulls feed on the shrimp. Moon-moths flutter over the flats at night.
reg_lustrine_shores.peoples: The people of the shores are glass-gatherers, lamp-makers, fishers and salt-panners. They are dreamy, superstitious and gentle, and their songs are slow and sad. Lustrine lamps, made of moon-glass, are sold across the world and never need oil.
reg_lustrine_shores.powerAndTrade: The villages are governed by their elders, and the glass-gatherers' guild controls the beaches. Moon-glass, lamps, salt and fish are traded abroad.
reg_lustrine_shores.faithAndCustoms: The people honour the day-gods and the moons, both of them. They believe the glass is the moon's tears, and they leave the largest pieces on the beach as offerings. They do not look at the red moon directly.

history.now: Ilyanthe has begun harvesting the light from the glass, and the beaches are going dark. Gatherers who are on the flats when she comes are found the next morning, pale and empty-eyed.
history.parents: Within living memory the first moon-glass washed ashore, and the shores went from poverty to prosperity in a generation.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the shores were poor fishing villages, and there was only one moon.
history.ancient: The glass began washing in after the red moon rose. The fishers' songs changed key that same year.

reg_lustrine_shores.tyrant: Ilyanthe, the Moon Harvester, is a vesperite, a creature from the red moon, who descends on the high tides to harvest the light from the moon-glass. She gathers it into a great lantern and carries it back up. She takes the light from people too, and she does not seem to know the difference.

settlements.name: Lustrine glass beaches
settlements.text: Villages on the dunes above the glowing beaches.

landmarks.name: The Glass Flats
landmarks.text: Miles of glowing glass revealed at low tide.

landmarks.name: The Lamp Market
landmarks.text: Where Lustrine lamps are made and sold.

landmarks.name: The Tide Stair
landmarks.text: A stair cut into the dunes where Ilyanthe descends.

hooks: A glass-gatherer's daughter has lost her light, and her mother wants it back.
A lamp-maker has made a lamp that glows red, and it is calling to something.
Scholars want a sample of the light Ilyanthe carries.
reg_lustrine_shores.senses: Salt and pine; the glitter of glass underfoot; slow sad songs; a red glow on the horizon.

reg_quaking_lands.name: Quaking Lands
reg_quaking_lands.summary: The ground here moves, and towns are built around the few springs where it is still. Quakeback is the reason, and it is turning in its sleep.
reg_quaking_lands.echo: The Stillers learned to read tremors the way sailors read weather. Their oldest maps are all wrong now.
reg_quaking_lands.overview: The Quaking Lands are a region of mountains and plains where the ground never stops moving. Hills shift, rivers change course overnight and new valleys open with a sound like thunder. The people who live here, the Stillers, have built their towns around the few springs where the ground is still. Quakeback, the Earthshaker Behemoth, is the reason, and it is turning in its sleep.
reg_quaking_lands.geography: The land is a broken country of ridges, cracks, landslides and new-made hills, between a range of jagged mountains and a broad, rippling plain. Rivers appear and disappear, and lakes drain overnight. The still springs are scattered across the region, each one a calm pool where the ground does not move, and every town is built around one. The Stillers' oldest maps show mountains that are no longer there.
reg_quaking_lands.ecology: Animals here are hardy and adaptable: burrowing creatures, mountain goats, wolves and birds that nest on the ground and can fly at the first tremor. Earth elementals and stone beasts thrive in the quakes. Plants grow fast and shallow, and the Stillers farm in quick seasons between tremors.
reg_quaking_lands.peoples: The Stillers are a resilient, patient people who read tremors the way sailors read weather. They build in wood and rope rather than stone, and every house can be taken down and moved in a day. They are calm in a crisis and nervous in calm weather.
reg_quaking_lands.powerAndTrade: Each spring-town is ruled by its tremor-readers, who decide when to farm, when to move and when to run. The towns trade tremor-charts, wood, herbs and the strange crystals the quakes bring up from below.
reg_quaking_lands.faithAndCustoms: The Stillers honour the day-gods and the still springs, which they consider sacred. They believe the earth is a sleeping beast and that the springs are where it has promised not to move.

history.now: Quakeback has begun to stir, and the tremors are stronger and more frequent. Two still springs have cracked, and their towns have had to flee.
history.parents: Within living memory a great quake split the plain and opened a valley that the Stillers still call the New Gorge.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the tremors were gentle and the springs were many.
history.ancient: The Stillers learned to read tremors the way sailors read weather. Their oldest maps are all wrong now.

reg_quaking_lands.tyrant: Quakeback, the Earthshaker Behemoth, is a creature so vast that the region's mountains are its back. It has slept beneath the Quaking Lands for ages, and its dreams make the ground move. Now it is waking, and every turn it makes reshapes the land. It does not know the Stillers exist.

settlements.name: Stiller spring-towns
settlements.text: Towns of wood and rope built around the still springs.

landmarks.name: The Still Springs
landmarks.text: Calm pools where the ground does not move.

landmarks.name: The New Gorge
landmarks.text: A valley opened by a great quake within living memory.

landmarks.name: Quakeback's Ridge
landmarks.text: A mountain ridge that breathes.

hooks: A tremor-reader has predicted a great quake, and no one believes her.
A spring-town needs to move, and the route crosses Quakeback's Ridge.
A Stiller child has learned to calm the tremors by singing to the ground.
reg_quaking_lands.senses: Dust and pine; the creak of rope houses; a constant faint vibration underfoot; the deep groan of the earth.

reg_aurumdeep.name: Aurumdeep
reg_aurumdeep.summary: A drowned underground kingdom of gold, now an explorers' camp at its edge. The Mad Magician who sank it is still performing.
reg_aurumdeep.echo: Aurumdeep was the richest kingdom on any map, until a single show-night sank it.
reg_aurumdeep.overview: Aurumdeep was the richest kingdom on any map: a realm of golden halls built into a great cavern beneath the earth, lit by enchanted lamps and fed by underground rivers. Then, on the night of the most famous magic show in history, the whole kingdom sank deeper into the earth, and the rivers poured in after it. Its golden streets lie flooded and dark, full of treasure and of the dead who never left their seats. An explorers' camp clings to the cavern's edge, and every season more treasure-hunters come down the Long Stair. The Mad Magician who sank the kingdom is still performing.
reg_aurumdeep.geography: The cavern of Aurumdeep is so large that clouds of mist form under its roof. The sunken city fills its floor: palaces, towers, bridges and avenues of gilded stone, flooded to different depths so that some streets are dry, some knee-deep and some lost under fathoms of clear, cold water. Enchanted lamps still burn in many of the halls, so the drowned city glows gold from beneath the surface. The explorers' camp sits on a broad ledge high on the cavern wall, at the foot of the Long Stair that winds up to the surface.
reg_aurumdeep.ecology: Blind white fish, cave eels and golden-shelled crabs have colonised the flooded streets, feeding on the algae that grows around the lamps. Bats roost under the cavern roof. The dead of Aurumdeep still walk the dry halls in their finest clothes, polite and confused, and the Magician's illusions wander everywhere: painted doves, silk dragons, smiling assistants that dissolve when touched. Nothing here is quite what it looks like, including the gold.
reg_aurumdeep.peoples: The camp is home to treasure-hunters, divers, scholars, fences, cooks and a handful of descendants of Aurumdeep's survivors, who were outside the kingdom on the night it sank and who consider the treasure-hunters grave-robbers. The explorers are brave, greedy and superstitious, and they trade stories as freely as gold. A diver's reputation rests on how deep she has gone and what she brought back.
reg_aurumdeep.powerAndTrade: An explorers' council governs the camp and sells diving rights to each district of the sunken city. Claim disputes are settled by the council, or in the water. Gold, gems, relics, books and enchanted lamps flow up the Long Stair, and food, rope, lamps and diving gear flow down it. The survivors' descendants petition every kingdom on the surface to declare Aurumdeep a tomb and close it; none has agreed.
reg_aurumdeep.faithAndCustoms: Explorers pray to Vex before every dive and leave a coin on the first step of the water for the dead. No one in the camp applauds, ever, for anything. The survivors' descendants hold a silent vigil on the anniversary of the sinking and leave a single empty seat at every table.

history.now: The Mad Magician's show has started again in the Golden Theatre, and explorers who stay to watch it are found the next day turned to gold, smiling in their seats.
history.parents: Within living memory the first explorers found the Long Stair, and the camp grew from a single tent to a town in a decade.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the survivors' families still spoke of Aurumdeep as home and refused to say what the Magician had promised the king that night.
history.ancient: Aurumdeep was the richest kingdom on any map, until a single show-night sank it.

reg_aurumdeep.tyrant: The Mad Magician of Aurumdeep, Sinker of Kingdoms, was the court magician of the golden kingdom. On the night of his greatest show he promised the king a trick that would make Aurumdeep the richest realm forever, and he performed it, and the kingdom sank. He has been performing ever since to an audience of the dead, waiting for applause that would end the trick. His illusions fill the city, and his greatest trick turns those who watch it into gold. He may be mad, cursed or simply unable to stop.

settlements.name: Aurumdeep explorers' camp
settlements.text: A rough town of tents, huts and cranes on a ledge above the sunken city, at the foot of the Long Stair.

landmarks.name: The Golden Theatre
landmarks.text: The theatre where the show is still performed to an audience of the dead.

landmarks.name: The Sunken Palace
landmarks.text: The king's palace, flooded to its upper floors, where the crown is said to still sit on the throne.

landmarks.name: The Long Stair
landmarks.text: The winding stair from the surface, with a memorial shrine at every hundredth step.

hooks: An explorer has been turned to gold in his seat at the theatre, and his partner wants him back before the fences carve him up.
A survivor's descendant wants to find out what trick the Magician promised, and believes the answer is in the theatre's prompt-book.
A diver claims to have seen the king alive in the Sunken Palace, sitting on his throne, waiting for the show to end.
reg_aurumdeep.senses: Cold clear water and the glint of gold; the echo of applause that never comes; dripping stone; the smell of old greasepaint and lamp oil.

reg_nox_dominion.name: Nox Dominion
reg_nox_dominion.summary: Volcanic ruinland under a dark sky, and the seat of the Demon Overlord's power. No Tyrant holds it, because the Dominion answers to someone far worse.
reg_nox_dominion.echo: The heroes of past ages marched here. The ruins remember them, and so do the statues.
reg_nox_dominion.overview: Nox Dominion is the volcanic heartland of the demon realms, a land of black rock, red rivers and ruined fortresses under a sky that is always dark. It is the seat of the Demon Overlord's power and the end of every hero's road. It is also, to the surprise of everyone who reaches it, a place where ordinary demons live ordinary lives: farmers, merchants, innkeepers and children, who fear the war as much as anyone. No Tyrant holds it, because the Dominion answers to someone far worse.
reg_nox_dominion.geography: The Dominion is a land of active volcanoes, lava rivers, ash plains and obsidian cliffs, under clouds of smoke that block the sun. The ruins of ancient fortresses, many built by armies that came to conquer it, stand on every ridge. At its centre stands the Overlord's citadel, a fortress of black stone on a mountain of fire. Border towns cling to the edges where the land is gentler.
reg_nox_dominion.ecology: Fire-adapted plants and fungi grow in the ash, and demon livestock graze on them. Hellhounds, salamanders, fire drakes and stranger creatures live in the wilds. The demons farm, hunt and trade like any other people.
reg_nox_dominion.peoples: The demons of Nox Dominion are as varied as any people: soldiers, farmers, merchants, artisans and scholars, cruel and kind, loyal and rebellious. Many fear the Overlord and his Generals, and some quietly oppose them. Human prisoners, deserters and traders also live in the border towns.
reg_nox_dominion.powerAndTrade: The Dominion is ruled by the Demon Overlord and his five Generals, each commanding a province and an army. Below them, demon nobles govern the towns. The economy rests on obsidian, sulphur, fire-crystals and war.
reg_nox_dominion.faithAndCustoms: The demons have their own gods and their own stories, and many of them honour the Overlord as a saviour. Some still pray to the day-gods in secret.

history.now: The war is reaching its climax, and the Dominion's armies are on the march. The border towns are full of refugees from both sides.
history.parents: Within living memory the Lantern Seal held the Overlord, and the Dominion knew a generation of uneasy peace.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the heroes of past ages marched here, and the ruins still bear their marks.
history.ancient: The heroes of past ages marched here. The ruins remember them, and so do the statues.

reg_nox_dominion.tyrant: Nox Dominion has no Tyrant and no siege; it is a story region. Its masters are the Demon Overlord and his Generals, and their story is told elsewhere.

landmarks.name: The Overlord's Citadel
landmarks.text: A fortress of black stone on a mountain of fire.

landmarks.name: The Hero's Road
landmarks.text: A path of ruined fortresses left by past heroes' campaigns.

landmarks.name: The Border Towns
landmarks.text: Towns at the Dominion's edge where demons and humans trade, home of the Crimson Rest.

hooks: A demon innkeeper is hiding a human deserter and wants help getting him home.
A demon child has run away to find out what humans are really like.
A ruined fortress holds a hero's statue, and something is wrong with its face.
reg_nox_dominion.senses: Sulphur and ash; the glow of lava rivers; the clang of forges; a sky that never brightens.

reg_calamity_steppe.name: Calamity Steppe
reg_calamity_steppe.summary: A steppe the size of a kingdom with no towns and no roads, where the monsters graze like herds. No one lives here to be besieged.
reg_calamity_steppe.echo: Calamities are born here and wander out. The guild charts their trails like rivers.
reg_calamity_steppe.overview: The Calamity Steppe is an immense grassland in the far west, the size of a kingdom, with no towns, no roads and no people. It belongs to the monsters, and the monsters here are the size of hills. They graze its grass and hunt one another in herds, and now and then one of them wanders east into the inhabited world and becomes a Calamity. The guild charts their trails like rivers. No Tyrant holds the steppe and no one lives there to be besieged; there is nothing to defend but your own life.
reg_calamity_steppe.geography: The steppe is a vast, rolling plain of tall grass that ripples like the sea, broken by lone hills, dry riverbeds, salt pans and craters left by battles between monsters. The grass grows so fast that trails close behind the herds within days. There are no trees for a hundred miles. In the middle of the steppe stand the Tusks, a ring of colossal bones, the remains of something that died here long ago and that every Calamity seems to visit at least once.
reg_calamity_steppe.ecology: The Calamity Steppe is an ecosystem of giants. Behemoths graze, titanic beasts hunt them and swarms of smaller monsters follow both to feed on the leftovers. The grass is rich in mana, which may be why the monsters grow so large. Birds as big as ships ride the thermals, and burrowing monsters tunnel beneath the plain. When a Calamity is born, a creature grown beyond the steppe's capacity to feed it, it walks east toward the lands of people.
reg_calamity_steppe.peoples: No one lives on the steppe. Expeditions of S-rank adventurers, scholars and guild cartographers cross it in armoured caravans, and a few hermits and madmen have tried to live there. The beastkin clans of Fanghold tell stories of their ancestors who walked the Calamity Steppe and came back changed.
reg_calamity_steppe.powerAndTrade: No power holds the steppe. The guild maintains watchtowers along its eastern edge to track Calamities as they leave it, and issues expedition licences only to the highest ranks.
reg_calamity_steppe.faithAndCustoms: The clans of the eastern steppes believe the Calamity Steppe is where the first monsters were made, and they leave offerings at its edge to keep them there. Guild cartographers have their own superstition: never name a monster on the steppe until you are off it.

history.now: The guild's watchtowers report more Calamities leaving the steppe this year than in any year on record, and all of them walking in the same direction.
history.parents: Within living memory a Calamity walked out of the steppe and flattened a city before it was killed, and the guild built the watchtowers in response.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the steppe's edge was a hundred miles further west.
history.ancient: Calamities are born here and wander out. The guild charts their trails like rivers.

reg_calamity_steppe.tyrant: The Calamity Steppe has no Tyrant and no siege, because there are no settlements to defend. Its monsters are the greatest wild creatures in the world, and some of them are greater than many Tyrants.

landmarks.name: The Tusks
landmarks.text: A ring of colossal bones in the middle of the steppe that every Calamity visits.

landmarks.name: The Watchtowers
landmarks.text: The guild's towers along the eastern edge, tracking Calamities as they leave.

landmarks.name: The Salt Pans
landmarks.text: White flats where the giants come to lick salt and fight.

hooks: A watchtower has gone silent, and the last report mentioned a Calamity walking toward it.
A scholar wants to know why every Calamity visits the Tusks.
A guild cartographer has named a monster on the steppe, and now it is following her.
reg_calamity_steppe.senses: Endless grass hissing in the wind; the ground trembling under distant footsteps; the smell of crushed herbs and old bone; a sky that feels too big.

reg_the_maw.name: The Maw
reg_the_maw.summary: A pit that breathes. The Hive Mother's world event begins here, and so does the swarm.
reg_the_maw.echo: The Maw opened after the Sundering, and the land around it has been sinking ever since.
reg_the_maw.overview: The Maw is a pit in the western lands that breathes. Air rushes in for an hour and out for an hour, as regular as a sleeper's breath, and the sound can be heard for miles. It descends into the Underworld deeper than anyone has measured, and the land around it has been sinking ever since it opened. It is home to the Hive Mother, and when she stirs the swarm pours out and becomes a world event that no single region can face alone.
reg_the_maw.geography: The Maw is a vast, round shaft hundreds of yards across, its walls ribbed like a throat and slick with a resinous coating. Tunnels branch off it at every depth, leading into a honeycomb of chambers that fills the rock for miles around. The land around the rim slopes inward and cracks as it sinks. At the bottom, far below where any lantern reaches, lies the Hive Mother's chamber.
reg_the_maw.ecology: The Maw is a single, enormous hive. Its insectoid creatures, the swarm, are all the Hive Mother's children: workers, soldiers, flyers and stranger castes that seem to be made for specific tasks. They harvest the surrounding land, carrying everything down into the pit. Nothing else lives near the Maw for long.
reg_the_maw.peoples: No one lives at the Maw. The guild maintains a fortified watch camp on a ridge some miles away, and S-rank parties occasionally descend to cull the swarm or study it.
reg_the_maw.powerAndTrade: No power holds the Maw. The guild coordinates the response when the swarm rises, and the kingdoms of the world are bound by treaty to send help.
reg_the_maw.faithAndCustoms: Some say the Maw is a mouth of the world itself, breathing in the sins of the surface. The guild's watchers simply count the breaths and grow nervous when the rhythm changes.

history.now: The Maw's breathing has quickened, and the guild watchers believe the Hive Mother is waking.
history.parents: Within living memory the swarm rose and stripped three provinces before the combined armies drove it back down.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the Maw was smaller, and its breath could barely be heard.
history.ancient: The Maw opened after the Sundering, and the land around it has been sinking ever since.

reg_the_maw.tyrant: The Maw has no Tyrant and no siege. Its Calamity, the Hive Mother, is a world event, not a regional siege, and when she rises the whole world must answer.

landmarks.name: The Rim
landmarks.text: The cracked, sinking edge of the pit, where the breath can knock a person over.

landmarks.name: The Watch Camp
landmarks.text: The guild's fortified camp on a ridge, counting the breaths.

landmarks.name: The Throat
landmarks.text: The upper shaft, ribbed and slick, where the swarm's tunnels begin.

hooks: The watch camp's breath-counter has noticed a second rhythm under the first.
An S-rank party went down to cull the swarm and has sent back only a single word.
A farmer near the Maw says his field sank a foot overnight, and something under it is singing.
reg_the_maw.senses: A wind that pulls and pushes; the hum of a million wings; resin and dust; the deep, slow breathing of something huge.

reg_root_of_the_world.name: Root of the World
reg_root_of_the_world.summary: The deepest place there is: roots of light and stone that hold the world above. Only the strongest monsters live this close to where the world was made.
reg_root_of_the_world.echo: Legends call it the place the gods knelt down to weave.
reg_root_of_the_world.overview: The Root of the World is the deepest place there is, far below the Underworld's other layers. Here vast roots of light and stone rise out of the darkness and hold up everything above: the Underworld, the surface, the seas and the sky. The air hums, the stone glows and the monsters are among the oldest and strongest in existence. No one lives here. Very few have ever come here and returned. Legends call it the place the gods knelt down to weave.
reg_root_of_the_world.geography: The Root is a cavern without visible walls or floor, crossed by immense pillars that seem to be both roots and stone, threaded with veins of light. Paths of rock wind between them, bridges of crystal span gulfs of nothing and islands of earth float in the dark. The light in the roots pulses slowly, like a heartbeat. Some of the roots are cracked, and light leaks from them like sap.
reg_root_of_the_world.ecology: Only elementals, aberrations, living plants, constructs, dragons and slimes survive here, the creatures that need no sun and can feed on raw mana. They cluster around the roots and drink the light that leaks from them. Some are so old that they seem to have forgotten what they were.
reg_root_of_the_world.peoples: No one lives at the Root. A few of the world's greatest adventurers have reached it, and they speak of it rarely and always with reverence.
reg_root_of_the_world.powerAndTrade: No power holds the Root. It belongs to whatever made the world.
reg_root_of_the_world.faithAndCustoms: Every faith in Aetheria has a story about the Root. The Church calls it the foundation stone of creation; the elves, the root of the World Tree; the dwarves, the first anvil. All of them agree that it should not be damaged, and that the cracks are a bad sign.

history.now: Adventurers who have reached the Root report that the cracks in the roots are widening and that the light leaking from them is growing brighter.
history.parents: Within living memory a party reached the Root for the first time in a century and brought back a shard of root-light that still glows in the Church's treasury.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the Root was thought to be a metaphor.
history.ancient: Legend says the gods knelt here to weave the world, and that their kneeling marks are still pressed into the stone.

reg_root_of_the_world.tyrant: The Root of the World has no Tyrant and no siege; it is the Underworld's deepest layer and holds no settlements. Its monsters are some of the oldest beings in creation.

landmarks.name: The Kneeling Stones
landmarks.text: Two great hollows in the rock, said to be where the gods knelt.

landmarks.name: The Cracked Root
landmarks.text: A root split from top to bottom, leaking light.

landmarks.name: The Crystal Bridges
landmarks.text: Bridges of crystal spanning bottomless gulfs.

hooks: The Church wants to know whether the shard in its treasury is growing.
A slime that has lived at the Root for an age has learned to speak, and it wants to tell someone what it saw.
An adventurer swears she heard someone weeping inside the Cracked Root.
reg_root_of_the_world.senses: A deep hum felt in the bones; the slow pulse of light; air like the inside of a bell; absolute, ancient stillness.

reg_vesper.name: Vesper
reg_vesper.summary: The red moon. After the war it opens for those strong enough to reach it.
reg_vesper.echo: Nobody on the surface remembers the moon being red before. Everyone remembers it red now.
reg_vesper.overview: Vesper is the red moon that hangs over Aetheria, and after the war is over it opens to those strong enough to reach it. Its surface is a broken landscape of ruins, crimson dust and floating stone, and its monsters are unlike anything on the world below. Nobody on the surface remembers the moon being red before; everybody remembers it red now. What lies at its heart is the last mystery of the world.
reg_vesper.geography: From the surface, Vesper is a red disc with darker marks like the outlines of streets. Up close, those marks are exactly that: the ruins of a city, broken and scattered across the moon's surface, some of it drifting in the sky above. The ground is red dust and shattered stone, and the sky is black with stars. The gravity is light, and the silence is complete.
reg_vesper.ecology: Vesperites, creatures born from the red moon's light, roam the ruins: some delicate, some monstrous, some almost human. The undead, shadows, aberrations, constructs and demons wander among them. Nothing grows here, but the ruins sometimes bloom with flowers of red light.
reg_vesper.peoples: No one is known to live on Vesper. Those who reach it report that they feel watched, and that the ruins seem to remember them.
reg_vesper.powerAndTrade: No power is known to hold Vesper.
reg_vesper.faithAndCustoms: Every faith in Aetheria fears the red moon. The Church calls it an omen; the elves, a wound in the sky; the fishers of the Lustrine Shores, a thief of light.

history.now: After the war, Vesper opens to those who can reach it, and the truth of the red moon waits at its heart.
history.parents: Within living memory the red moon's light has drawn vesperites down to the Lustrine Shores.
history.grandparents: In their grandparents' time the scholars began to argue about the marks on the red moon's face, and why they looked like streets.
history.ancient: Nobody on the surface remembers the moon being red before. Everyone remembers it red now.

reg_vesper.tyrant: Vesper has no Tyrant and no siege; it is the post-game region. What waits there belongs to the end of the story.

landmarks.name: The Broken Streets
landmarks.text: Ruins of a city scattered across the moon's surface.

landmarks.name: The Floating Quarter
landmarks.text: Fragments of the city drifting in the black sky above.

landmarks.name: The Red Heart
landmarks.text: The centre of the moon, where the light is strongest.

hooks: A scholar's map of the marks on the red moon matches a city on no map of the world.
A vesperite has followed an adventurer back to the surface and is trying to find someone.
The red flowers that bloom in the ruins sing a song that an old woman in Aldmere recognises.
reg_vesper.senses: Silence and red dust; starlight without air; flowers of light opening in the ruins; the feeling that the city remembers you.
